newsitem.title: USA: Cargill awaits Treasury decision on North Korea trade.
newsitem.headline: Cargill awaits Treasury decision on North Korea trade.

text.p: Cargill Inc is waiting for a decision from the Treasury Department on an application to sell up to 2 million metric tons of grain to North Korea, a Cargill spokeswoman said on Monday.

The application, submitted in September, "includes a broad authorization on what constitutes the business and does not specify rice, corn or other commodity. But it would be food," Cargill spokeswoman Laurie Johnson told Reuters.

"The license application is set up to allow a maximum of 2 million tons of grains. It is now in the hands of the Treasury Department, as to whether to permit the business, volumes, and so on," Johnson said.
Minneapolis-based Cargill is the world's largest private grain trading company.
"Whether we get the license or not, one of the significant issues that remains to be addressed is finance," Johnson said.
The official North Korean news agency KCNA said on Monday the United States had pledged to ease a trade embargo against North Korea and give food aid to the communist state.
The reclusive North Korea has been suffering from famine after two consecutive years of serious flooding.
Officials and diplomats close to U.S.-North Korean talks in New York said Sunday the U.N. World Food Program plans to issue another appeal for North Korean aid in the next few weeks.
They said Washington may pledge $6 million worth of food aid and in addition could issue a license to allow Cargill to export 500,000 tons of food in a barter transaction.
On Sunday, North Korea apologized for the first time for an incursion by one of its submarines into South Korean waters in September, expressing "deep regret" in a brief statement.
It also expressed willingness to discuss its nuclear fuel program and a framework for regional peace talks.
President Clinton called North Korea's apology a "significant development, which I hope will contribute to the reduction of tensions on the Korean peninsula."
